history.summary: SPELLING NOTE: sources variously give Trineshwara, Trinesvara, Trinayaneshvara and Trinesvaraswamy; the CSV spelling 'Trinesvaraswamy' matches usage in travel media. The temple predates Raja Wodeyar (r.1569+) and originally stood on the Devaraya Sagar (Doddakere) bank outside the fort; it came inside the fort enclosure when Kanthirava Narasaraja Wodeyar (1638-1659) and Dodda Devaraja Wodeyar (1659-1672) enlarged the fort. Kanthirava added a verandah and consecrated five lingas; the lofty mahadwara gopura was destroyed in the 18th century. An 11-kg gold mask (Chinnada Kolaga), donated by Maharaja Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar in 1953, adorns the linga on Mahashivaratri. One of the ASI-protected temples within the Amba Vilas Palace fort group.

name: Trineshwara Swamy Temple
town_description: Mysuru (Mysore) in southern Karnataka was the royal capital of the Wodeyar dynasty and is famous for the Amba Vilas Palace, Chamundi Hill and its Dasara celebrations.

travel.airport: Mysuru Airport (~12 km); Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~170 km)
travel.railway: Mysuru Junction (~2-3 km); auto-rickshaws and city buses available
travel.road: Inside the Mysuru Palace fort complex, Agrahara-KR Mohalla; combine with a Mysuru Palace visit

visitor_information.best_time: Mahashivaratri for the gold-mask ritual; February for Rathotsava; early mornings year-round
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-7:00 PM (per ZeeZest travel guide; verify)
